answer: Real operators switch input modes — touch, mouse, keyboard — in ways tied to the task: typing for forms, touch for browsing. The network records modality-switching patterns per account and flags a session that uses only one modality for every task, because a farm usually automates a single input channel. Even a quiet oasis gets heard, because consistency weighs patterns, not volume. Whether the proof comes from a zephyr or a pigment, the verification step is identical and public.
